pages.title: Agnes
text: The fires that burned down the great City of Arcadia have long since faded. The only ones who remember them belong to the Phaethon military machine that destroyed "utopia" and the few survivors like Agnes who escaped alive. She still dreams about the fire most nights. The pain inflicted by Phaethon still lingers deep in her heart. Still she wishes to rebuild the ancient city. Still she wishes for revenge against the war machine that left those scars. Whenever Agnes is tempted to give up in the face of evil she remembers her mission. She is one of the greatest scientists on the Tundra, a brave leader who today partners with the Dawn Alliance in their grandest project: to rebuild New Arcadia as she remembers it. It will be a perfect utopia that shall never again suffer the fate of its namesake. Agnes has welcomed many fellow refugees throughout the years all with the eventual goal of resettling "New Arcadia". So large has the group grown, Agnes was asked to leave her last City which was unable to provide enough heat to accommodate all of her survivors. But in New Arcadia this will never be an issue. New Arcadia will utilize the greatest furnace known to man: an old volcano. The idea has been laughed at by some, called impossible by others, but those like Logan who know Agnes well know that if Agnes says they can safely use volcanic heat, that is exactly what they will do. The New Arcadia has been built largely according to Agnes' vision, a city that treasures the arts, humanities, music, and takes pride in its largest central building consisting of a grand library dedicated to the improvement of the world through knowledge. The old Arcadians used to say: "Only a beautiful world is worth protecting". Agnes holds similar ideals today. Others like Flint consider it a fool's errand to try to build utopia on Earth. Not Agnes. Agnes aims for a greatness she associates with the old world of the past. Yet Agnes is determined that the New Arcadia will not walk in the ways of the old. She has seen to it that New Arcadia boasts a very large standing army. The City certainly needs it. A Phaethon legion has already been assigned to subjugate New Arcadia for the sake of its precious knowledge, and one of the largest group of bandits on the Tundra has encamped nearby. Two menacing armies on the new City's doorstep are a constant source of stress for the inhabitants. For Agnes, it is a crisis that cannot be wasted. If only these two birds could be killed with one stone! But Agnes will need help—help from a strong and enterprising Chief perhaps...

pages.title: Justus
text: Justus, once the royal counselor to Princess Eleonora of the Solaris Dynasty, was renowned for his wisdom and impartiality. While Sir Gregory trained Eleonora to become a formidable swordswoman, Justus shaped her into a respected and capable ruler.

Years earlier, Justus had witnessed the dynasty's downfall, brought about by the nobility's extravagance and cruelty. The empire's collapse left him devastated, enlightening him that a true ruler must protect the people and earn their loyalty through honor rather than privilege.
From that day onward, Justus devoted himself to guiding Eleonora according to the principles of kingship he held dear.

He found great comfort in watching her grow into a compassionate leader, a quality her father had never possessed. Perhaps her years in exile had opened her eyes to the hardships of ordinary people, or perhaps kindness had always been part of her nature. Whatever the reason, it was this compassion that convinced Justus she could one day build and lead the ideal kingdom he had always envisioned.

Together, Justus and Eleonora established shelters for those who had lost their homes. They worked alongside the people to build new settlements and tirelessly defended them from marauders. Under Justus's guidance, Eleonora's reputation quickly spread far and wide. To him, a good name was more valuable than any fortune in such turbulent times.
But fame often breeds resentment...

Baron Cassian, the sworn enemy of Eleonora and Justus, despised their belief in sharing the people's hardships and longed to reclaim the privileges of the old nobility. Choosing ambition over loyalty, he turned to betrayal. He also coveted the legendary lost royal treasure. Recently, he bribed one of Eleonora's attendants and repeatedly orchestrated plots that placed the princess in danger. Fortunately, a fearless chief and a brave adventurer intervened in time to foil his schemes.
After thwarting Cassian's plot, Justus began working with the chief's city, lending his expertise in governance to support its development.

Justus is fluent in a nearly forgotten ancient language, allowing him to communicate with the underground inhabitants more effectively and learn more about the underground world. pages.title: Gareth
text: The mountains of Jarnvid are home to many legendary warriors, but none more famous than Commander Gareth, prince and son of the High Chief.
From childhood, every son of Jarnvid is trained to wield spear and lance. Their fierce resolve and unbreakable brotherhood make them feared warriors both at home and abroad.
Even among these champions, Gareth stood out as a gifted young commander. Enemies who dismissed him as a mere mountain barbarian quickly learned how deadly his tactics could be.

Jarnvid's fate changed after vast resource deposits were discovered deep within the mountains. The newfound riches sparked conflict with neighboring plains tribes led by Chief Mordheim. Though none could rival Gareth in battle, their growing greed drove them down the path of war.

Though heavily outnumbered, Gareth never faltered. The plains warriors faced mountain fighters raised with spear in hand, masters of the harsh terrain where danger could strike from anywhere. For the first time, the mountain clans stood fully united.

Many of Mordheim's warriors fell before ever seeing their enemy. Others caught only a glimpse of the spiked Jarnvid banner before death claimed them. Soon, tales spread of Gareth's unstoppable defenses and the fearsome chief who fought like a wrathful god.

Driven to desperation, Chief Mordheim gathered a massive coalition army. Whatever price he paid to unite them remains unknown. Yet Gareth was ready, meeting the overwhelming force with a bold new strategy.

Long ago, Jarnvid had defended its alliance with the Dawn Alliance in blood, and that debt would not be forgotten in Jarnvid's darkest hour. What began with a brave chief and a daring explorer ended in victory over the invading horde, forging a lifelong friendship and alliance. In return, Gareth's leadership would help raise that chief's city to greatness.

Gareth enjoys great prestige among tribesmen. pages.title: Kathy
text: A daughter of Frostfire miners herself, the knowhow, courage and skills of Orichalcum mining were seared into Kathy's bones from a young age. A natural-born leader, it was not long before Kathy found herself leading her own crew where her instinct for danger and strong sense of compassion served everyone well. If challenges out here were only of the geological kind, mining at Frostfire would be bad enough. But Orichalcum's usefulness attracts more dangerous threats: bandits or, if Kathy is unlucky, more organized evils. She and her men have learned how to work a sword and shield as well as any drill. Kathy's caring, well-run operation is seen by the Dawn Alliance as a breath of fresh air in a cutthroat industry, and earned the respect of Dawn leaders like Logan. In Kathy, the Dawn Alliance sees a natural ally willing to put people above profits and in return they have worked to secure her much better mining equipment. But Kathy's outfit has never been the largest in Frostfire. That honor belongs to Antaeus' crew and his mysterious backers who have funded him with every advance in technology plus a heavily armed mercenary force. Antaeus has been the chief antagonist in Frostfire since he arrived with the hostility of a whirlwind. When Antaeus' offer to buy out all the other sites were rejected, he turned to less peaceful means. Antaeus' mercenaries overran the less well-defended crews. But Frostfire also has a habit of swallowing up people that do not respect its unpredictable ways. Kathy and her ragtag allies worked with the earthquake-prone terrain to snatch victory from the jaws of defeat. An uneasy truce was established... but everybody knew it could not last. Once again, chaos has come to Frostfire Mine. This time, a series of earthquakes has caved in many sites. Only Antaeus seems protected—allegedly they are the only crew able to repel the "Ancient One". Frostfire has always been heavy with rumors of a great underground beast who stirs the earth. Each stirring brings fresh quakes, tragedy, and ruin. Antaeus claims only his mines are outfitted with a kind of "beast repellent" that prevents the entity from approaching his sites. For many small-time crews, this promise of protection was the last straw required to force them to sign on Antaeus' dotted line—even if his wages aren't nearly as good. Kathy has heard about legendary entities since she was old enough to sit by a campfire, and has never once believed them. Kathy's instincts led her down a very different path and to the real culprit of the disasters, but she could not have done so without the help of a trustworthy Chief and Explorer. In return, a grateful Kathy has agreed to lend her vast expertise to the lucky Chief's own City.

pages.title: Ronne
text: Ronne has a great name in the mercenary field, but even greater among employers who enjoy her almost reckless shock-and-awe tactics. Even these are no more than a calculated strategy by a lady far more cunning than her enemies realize. Ronne's no-holds-barred style of offensive is only another ploy to drive enemies away without the cost of a battle. Therein the real legend of Ronne lies. The mercenary world has recently had to bid farewell to this artisan of aggression, as she has traded her mercenary general's banner for a heavily armored and armed caravan vehicle. The merchant bodyguard life offers Ronne what the mercenary life could not : greater-than-mercenary wages with merchant convoy-levels of danger. The opening of massive Tundra trade routes has been a time of great enrichment for just about everyone. This includes bandits — who would like nothing more than to violently redirect money flowing between cities into their own pockets. Sometimes the risk of a raid is just too great. especiallv for bigger convoys. And where there are deep pockets, there are plenty of opportunities for ex-mercenaries like Ronne. Ronne is one of few guards-for-hire with a flawless track record, no matter the value of the cargo she and her men have escorted. Ronne's bravery, experiences, and skills all go toward making her expensive, very expensive. Ronne never wastes a moment to add to her arsenal and has been known to tinker with mechanical contraptions for an extra edge. Her ability to turn broken vehicles into primitive tanks, repair cargo-movers on the fly—not to mention the machine guns and armor she installs—are legendary. With Ronne, any old four wheels on a chassis can become a hulking road-monster. Now this monster also has one of the best drivers on the Tundra: Ronne, Queen of the Convoys. Lately, though, it has not been the bandits causing Ronne the most grief, but ironically the tension within: public safety versus cargo some would consider dangerous and unethical. It is largely because of the helpful Explorer who allowed Ronne to extricate herself from this delicate situation with her honor unscathed that has seen her join his Chief's City. There, she uses her experiences, skills, and knowledge of the Tundra trade routes to help the Explorer's mighty Chief do even more good.

pages.title: Holger
text: Ace of the Arena, undefeated champion for many years and winner of numerous trophy cups, Holger's future was once very bright. A combination of professional negligence, lax rules, and evil cunning tragically put that future to an end. None of the officials witnessed the poison dagger Conrad slipped into Holger's ribs as the two wrestled on the ground. Was it against Arena rules? Certainly. Did it put an end to Holger's championship streak? Yes. Did it stop Conrad from winning the cup? Not at all. Conrad was back to competing for the trophy a few months later while Holger had to rest in bed in a long process of recovery that might take years. Time passed. Holger's trophies began to rust. His exploits began to fade from memory. Holger will never again be champion of the Arena, but Holger is still learning how much he has to teach. What is an Ace of the Arena to do after he has lost his crown? It was hard for Holger to accept he might never recover from his injuries. Life became quiet. Quiet, still, even a little bit... pointless. The fire of Holger's passion was fading until he saw the news: his old enemy Conrad had also retired from the Arena to coach. Holger almost had to thank Conrad for providing him with the inspiration for his next venture—if he wasn't still so filled with rage. Conrad revealed in an interview that he had nothing but contempt for old Holger and made no mention of the little present he slipped into Holger's ribs during their last battle. Holger could not believe his eyes. Such dishonor in one man... Yet Conrad was still a champion in the people's eyes. Better than defeating Conrad physically would be defeating him in the arena of honor. Holger would best Conrad at his own game: the art of training and coaching. Holger's championship era may be a distant memory, but his influence remains in all kinds of ways: from the strategies today's arena participants favor to modern-day formations, weapons, and combat approaches. That same creativity makes coaching difficult. The ageing champion has only attracted an uncertain few contenders without proven abilities. To say that it is going to be difficult even for Holger to make champions out of this "riffraff" is an understatement. Holger has tried to acquire better students more appreciative of the combat arts. His old friends at the Arena cannot help. They refuse to supply their best and brightest up-and-comers. Holger's angry dark side is well-known in the industry. A supremely gifted fighter, Holger could never win against his greatest enemy: himself. Knowing when to retreat can be half the battle. Holger's inability to say no to a challenge was what Conrad exploited in their final face-off. Holger could have rested, recovered and returned next season. By battling on despite blow after blow, Holger destroyed his health and career. Can a Holger unable to resist the path of anger be worthy of the best Arena students? But Holger is eager to prove himself, especially seeing the new Icebreaker Cup announcement. A friend in need is a friend indeed. Fortunately for Holger, a brave Chief might just be willing to extend the hand of friendship at this crucial time.

pages.title: Cyrille
text: Cyrille is one of those hunters whose exploits have spread far beyond her original City by tall tales, some of which are even true. It is true that when she was a teenager she survived a close encounter with a raging bear on her own. It is also true that after more than two decades hunting on the Tundra she has killed countless apex predators. If the beasts had any sense they would surely warn each other to beware of where the huntress treads. One of the reasons that Cyrille's legend might be perhaps more well-known is that she has kind heart and is dedicated to protecting survivors and the boundaries of different outposts. Her kindness is legendary in a land where every traveler feels like an island, well-informed by the horrid aftermath of claws and fangs on unfortunate survivors. Years of experience have given Cyrille an understanding of all the major predators' weaknesses and habits which she uses to great effect, especially against the raging bear. Cyrille has pioneered many new bear traps, exploding arrowheads, and tactics. She also fears what these giant super-predators represent: a distorted form of life that has flourished since the collapse of the old world and warning about what might happen if humanity lets its guard down. Cyrille often travels together with her friend Cloris, with whom she has an unspoken mentoring relationship. Cyrille first encountered Cloris running for her life through a snowstorm and assumed she had been separated from a hunting party. Little did she realize Cloris was not lost but hiding. The noise of the bandits' makeshift snowmobiles came roaring through the blinding snow. They were surrounded. Time was running out. It would be the first time Cyrille would have to spill human blood, but the experience did not affect her much. For the blood of a bandit who preys on the innocent and the blood of a wild beast is not too different in Cyrille's eyes. Reports of large-scale attacks against cities by even larger beasts worry Cyrille. Most attacks happen at night. Even where there are witness, no one seems to be able to exactly identify the creatures responsible. Nor are any usable tracks left behind—unless the animal is clever enough to conceal its movements. Either way, Cyrille's curiosity is piqued by this new threat to civilization. So when so many survivors are looking for answers, Cyrille may find herself working alongside a new Chief with a bold enough vision for how to put a stop to this threat.

pages.title: Fabian
text: Fabian had already found his calling at the grand Imperial Foundry as a young engineer. Corrupt and decadent though the old Solaris Empire was, Fabian's instructors could still be amazed at the young man's extraordinary talent for applied science. Ever the hothead, Fabian followed in the footsteps of his classmates to the Rebels when the evils of the nobility became too tyrannical to ignore. Here, talents nurtured by the Empire returned to them with devastating effectiveness thanks to the increasingly famous "Master of Arms" Fabian. The mostly older cohort of Imperial loyalists were sorely outmatched by the kind of firepower the young upstart was willing to bring onto the battlefield —especially when he went to test it himself! After doing more than his fair share to bring down the old Empire under the combined weight of the peasants' anger, Fabian could have practically asked for anything from the new government. Instead, he left the Rebels at the peak of his fame to begin a much quieter, simpler life with his new family. Months passed, then years, then a decade flew by in Fabian's happy family life in their cold new world. And then disaster! A sudden storm wiped out more than half of the inhabitants of Fabian's City, including his dear wife and children. There was no greater sorrow for Fabian than this. In the midst of raging despair, Fabian threw himself like a madman into his work: protecting survivors from other such calamities with his new inventions. Customers' orders began to flow. Skill created success. Success attracted attention. Attention attracted Fabian's wealthiest client yet, an old duke from the Solaris Empire who had since become a mighty Chief. Fabian's new client seemed to have infinite money and ambitions to match: ideas of a fortress on wheels. One that could safely transport survivors through any kind of storm or hazard! As the Chief would often remind Fabian, only he was capable of creating such a life-saving marvel. This was Fabian's grandest project. It only took several years and the invention of several new technologies before the grand "Typhon Tank" could be created. Tank by name, it may more accurately described as a fortress on treads. Imperial Foundry teachers would have cried to behold such a work of mechanical genius. No sooner had Fabian handed his Typhon over to the duke did he discover the awful truth: he was no City Chief, but a senior officer in Phaethon's tyrannical army. And what he had handed over were the keys to destroying any City on the Tundra, a wonder weapon to transform Phaethon into an indestructible whirlwind of suffering. Fabian had committed a terrible wrong. Surely he had not helped the Rebels take down an empire only to cement the dominance of their evil kin decades later? It was reason enough for Fabian to throw himself into the development of new and more powerful weapons which, unlike the Typhon, are less capable of large-scale death and destruction. His latest passion projects include armor-piercing artillery and bombs of all kinds. For Fabian has vowed to undo his latest and greatest mistake. Yet some might say what he really needs is a brave and just Chief willing to partner with this strange inventor.

pages.title: Romulus
text: Commander Romulus lived most of his life in a different world as a highly-decorated general in the old Solaris Empire's Royal Academy, a privileged leader with an upright reputation for integrity. Romulus' fall from grace happened not with the Great Chill, but much earlier. Over the years the nobility had become more powerful with the constant acquisition of land and titles, and one day Romulus woke up to find himself on their bad side. "Where there's smoke there's fire!" so the old saying goes, and rumors of Romulus' association with seditious rebels was enough for the king to remove Romulus in disgrace. But the same power that allowed nobles to remove a decorated hero like Romulus was the same power that allowed them to crush the life out of the peasants. Impossible taxes sparked the flame of rebellion first in the hinterlands and then closer to the heart of empire. This rebellion was big enough to wake up even the sheltered aristocracy within their bubble of wealth. In the time of their desperation, the old King thought of his former general the Court had mistreated years ago. Romulus returned at the head of an army of Loyalists and pitched camp against a vastly bigger army on the Rebel side. Romulus held the Rebels at bay for months, but soon realized his strategy was doomed to fail. The Rebel ranks kept increasing with discontented peasants as more and more Loyalists abandoned the cause. Battle was inevitable and, as expected, Romulus lost. So the general, twice elevated and twice disgraced, was led away in chains as a prisoner of war. Although an enemy of the Rebels, General Romulus had done nothing deserving of death. Many Rebels had once served under him, including the former student who currently commanded the main Rebel force. Romulus' chains were immediately removed and he was surprised to find he was being treated quite hospitably. Romulus spent months captive in the Rebel camp as he pondered his situation. Why should he fight on behalf of corrupt nobles uninterested in improving the life of the people? If the Rebels were going to win, why should he be numbered with the royal transgressors? Sunfire Castle fell to the Rebels in weeks. The royal family was no more. Romulus decided that for the sake of the new government that must rise in its place he would take the position of advisor to the Rebel leader who now called himself "Chief". Romulus found himself essentially a free man afterward, troubled only by one central question: what happened to the Aeetes? This was the brigade Romulus had founded and led for most of his career. Fearful of Romulus' unproven loyalty, the King had not allowed Romulus to return to his former command even when asked to fend off the Rebels. The Aeetes themselves were assigned as far away from Romulus as possible on the other side of the Imperial hinterland. Even the new Rebel government did not know what had happened to those Romulus once counted his closest friends. Romulus has retreated from public life and in the twilight of his years wishes to embark on a new and potentially very dangerous quest: to find out what happened to his old brothers-in-arms.

pages.title: Baldur
text: Baldur is a diplomat of the Dawn Alliance. Some call him astute, others conniving, and yet others inscrutable-but it is precisely these qualities that allow him to balance the interests of his allies, maximizing their strategic interests far beyond the battlefield! Given Baldur's exceptional eloquence and erudition, many assume that he descends from the noble class of the Solaris Dynasty. He claims, however, to be nothing more than an ordinary survivor. His familiarity with working-class devices such as the pulverizer and forging bench seems to corroborate this, while his knowledge and skills from the libraries of the Dawn Alliance and the survival techniques he learned through arduous years of hardship amidst the tundra. Beyond diplomacy and negotiation, Baldur also excels at combat. His swordsmanship was once tested against the great Jeronimo, and likewise, his marksmanship was measured against Bahiti, earning him only praise from both masters. These combat skills were not only for show-they have saved him from more than a few assassination attempts. It stands to reason that the purpose of war is to gain an advantage. Possessing a deep knowledge of this principle, Baldur could defuse rage-fueled potential wars by appealing to the mutual interests of all parties. Recently, he was tasked to mediate a conflict between two powerful lords. The dispute was triggered by unexpected news that sparked an argument over succession. To spare the common folk from the ravages of war, he had to uncover the truth behind a late lord's conflicting final wills. Guillaume and Hilmar were legendary warriors under Ambrosios the Lion. Ambrosios left no heirs, so upon his death, his two trusted lieutenants divided his lands equally. More recently, however, they each received differing copies of his "final will" with each copy designating them as the sole heir. And thus, the flame of conflict was kindled. Baldur's initial intervention delayed the simmering tide of war. Then, assisted by Bahiti, he fought the clock to uncover the mastermind behind the false, forged wills. In heir. And thus, the flame or conflict was kindled. Baldur's initial intervention delayed the simmering tide of war. Then, assisted by Bahiti, he fought the clock to uncover the mastermind behind the false, forged wills. In the end, the combined efforts of Baldur and Bahiti healed the rift between the two embattled lords, allowing them to join forces to defeat their mutual adversary, who had sought to profit from their enmity. After calming the crisis shoulder-to-shoulder, the friendship between the diplomat and the explorer had grown much more profound.

pages.title: Valeria
text: Valeria of the Dawnbreaker Brigade is an extremely talented commander, known for her versatile mastery of textbook Imperial tactics and leading one of the largest armies the Tundra has ever seen. The Brigade has been very friendly with the Dawn Alliance during Valeria's leadership, especially after her defense of several Cities during Phaethon's River of Rage invasion. This battle has been called Valeria's "impossible victory" where she held off a much larger, better-equipped Phaethon force by using the local terrain to her advantage. Valeria never intended to serve in the so-called Dawnbreaker Brigade or any other resistance against imperial authority. Nor did she expect to be serving alongside so many knights drawn from the lower social classes or their commoner brethren. The daughter of a noble family with military aspirations, Valeria's presence shows the apple has indeed fallen very far from the tree. Now Valeria has become the key to the Brigade's survival on many occasions. Valeria's hometown of Altea is the only Imperial city in the Empire to endure the Collapse. Many noble families took refuge there, Valeria's among them. There, Valeria completed her training with high honors, raising hopes that she might one day help the Alteans reclaim the Tundra under the glorious banner of Empire. Valeria had doubts about the Altean aristocracy for a long time. What right had they to rule Altea so brutally? Did rebellion really merit punishment worse than death? The human cost of Altean power chilled Valeria to her core. Its horrors were behind Valeria's decision to throw her lot in with "rebels" and bid farewell to endless bloodshed. Leaving Altea was no easy feat, but Valeria eventually found her way to the Dawnbreakers. Valeria has tried to avoid raising her sword against former countrymen, but that was then and this is now. Altea's ambitions grow ever greater. Many Cities near Valeria's Dawnbreakers have now been swept up in the carnage of Altea's dreams of empire. With so many Cities ransacked and their survivors pressed into servitude, the time has come for Valeria to make another difficult decision. She is well and truly involved in the battle for her life, and it has proved more complex than she dared imagine. Fortunately, she has had the benefit of a kind Chief who has taken courageous steps to resolve this latest crisis.
